_description: E-069 the cone-native codec itself — ConeMAE, the encoder that reads the INNER DEPENDENCY CONE (the lag-0 3x3 patch plus, per channel, a sunflower of dots at lags 1-6 pentads whose reach follows that channel's physics) instead of one snapshot, so a displacement can be inside the embedding rather than rebuilt from compressed codes downstream. This is the recipe f4r3-cone-5M.json said it could not be: every cone flag is now a `# recipe-only:` key of .github/workflows/ml-train.yml, consumed exactly once in the Train step's cone branch, so naming this recipe with `window: recipe:f4r3-cone-7M,cone` runs ml/train_cone.py with this geometry and nothing is left to a dispatch field somebody forgot. Geometry: Perceiver, 64 latents x d_model 256 x 6 blocks, 8 heads, decoder 256 x 2, Gaussian head, auxiliary loss through the decoder's full memory at weight 0.25 (the headline term always goes through z alone), 256 dot queries per anchor, future lags 1 and 2, inner window L_in = 6 pentads = 30 days. d_z 32 and batch 256 match the f4r2 codec family so a cone z and a snapshot z are the same width. cone_velocity_probe is true because a codec trained without H1's read-out is a run that answers nothing; cone_snapshot_ablation is TRUE here: H1 is read as the cone codec's velocity R-squared AGAINST its own L_in = 0 snapshot twin (E-069 handover section 6), and a run without the twin cannot answer H1 at all; the twin roughly doubles the wall clock, which is the price of a readable number. HEAD_PROBE IS 'true' EXPLICITLY as every recipe states it (ml/CLAUDE.md section 3: unpooled is the verdict), even though a cone run skips the probe phase entirely: the key records what the configuration says, and scripts/probes_run.sh is what decides that this run has no Z to probe.
_provenance: E-069 plan and handover, 2026-09-03. NOTHING HAS BEEN MEASURED ON THIS CONFIGURATION — no cone codec has been trained on an ocean tensor, and family4_na025_pentad_r3 has not itself been built or published, so a dispatch naming this recipe builds the tensor on the box unless handover section 4 (Phase A) has already published and pinned it. The one number here that IS measured is the parameter count: tests/test_jaxport_cone.py's C10 gate rebuilds this exact geometry at the r3 tensor's 42 channels and asserts BOTH the torch ConeMAE and its JAX port hold exactly 7,048,994 parameters (7.05M) over 748 tokens per anchor; tests/test_cone_smoke.py carries the same figure. Every other expectation attached to this recipe is a pre-registered prediction of the plan (H1: ridge R2 from a frozen z to cur_u/cur_v at the anchor, 0.3-0.6 for the cone against < 0.1 for the snapshot twin), not a result, and is owed to its first run. The 5M in the sibling f4r3-cone-5M.json's name is not this model at all: that recipe is the 40M-class PixelMAE snapshot control on the same tensor, and it is kept as it is.
